parts.text: A student investigates a light-dependent resistor (LDR). The student assembles a series circuit consisting of a power supply, a switch, a 470 Ω resistor and an LDR.

parts.label: a
parts.text: (a) Fig. 2.1 shows part of the circuit that the student assembles. Fig. 2.1 Complete the circuit by adding the correct symbol for an LDR between Y and Z. Choose from the list provided in Fig. 2.2. Fig. 2.2 [1]

ms.label: 2(a)
ms.text: correct symbol only for the LDR chosen AND a series connection

parts.label: i
parts.text: (b) (i) The student: • closes the switch • connects a voltmeter across the 470 Ω resistor • records the reading on the voltmeter • opens the switch. On Fig. 2.1, draw a voltmeter connected to measure the potential difference (p.d.) across the 470 Ω resistor. [1]

ms.label: 2(b)(i)
ms.text: correct voltmeter symbol AND voltmeter connected in parallel with the resistor

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The voltmeter reading is shown in Fig. 2.3. Fig. 2.3 Record the voltmeter reading V XY . V XY = ...................................................... V [1]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The current I in the circuit is calculated using the equation: I = V XY R , where R = 470 Ω. Use your voltmeter reading in (b)(ii) to calculate the current I. I = ......................................................... [2]

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) The student: • closes the switch • connects the voltmeter between points Y and Z • records the voltmeter reading V YZ • opens the switch. 2.2 V V YZ = ............................................................... Calculate the resistance R B of the LDR in bright light using the equation: R B = V YZ I . R B = ..................................................... Ω [1]

ms.label: 2(d)
ms.text: RB = 1290 OR 1292 OR 1292.5 OR 1293 OR 1294 OR 1300 (Ω) OR 2.2 ÷ candidate’s (c)

parts.label: i
parts.text: (e) (i) The student covers the LDR with a piece of card and repeats the procedure described in (b) and (d). 0.15 V V XY = ............................................................... 2.9 V V YZ = ............................................................... Calculate the resistance R D of the LDR in the dark using the equation: R D = 470 Ω × V YZ V XY . R D = ..................................................... Ω [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) The student removes the card from the top of the LDR and slowly lifts it vertically upwards away from the LDR until the card is 30 cm above the LDR. The student observes and records the readings on the voltmeter across the LDR (V YZ ) as the card is raised. Table 2.1 shows the student’s results.
